notes: Complete jobs retain runtime row source, row blackhole sink, both row/Arrow transposes, production IPC, JNI, Calc serialization and aggregate state. No build, test or other benchmark ran concurrently. Every candidate trial asserts native aggregation, both transposes and consumed native rows; prior trials enable the native planner and assert zero substitutions.

ONE_PHASE, mini-batching disabled, 1024-row transposes. Each fresh profile JVM runs two warmups and three measured trials per engine, alternating execution order. Cluster creation is outside timing; complete planning/submission/execution remains timed. No startup subtraction.

Character values are 16 bytes, drawn from sixteen values, NULL every seventh source row. BIGINT argument is the grouping key cast to BIGINT. Each row has a distinct string sort key. Retracting input cycles insert/insert/delete by key round; deletion matches the preceding inserted value and sort key.

ASC and DESC are inline JSON_ARRAYAGG order clauses. Flink 2.2.1 and 1.18.1 ignore these clauses for array sorting, retaining arrival order. The candidate matches that released behavior; it does not implement sorted aggregation.

Frozen original production code and native library are unchanged; only the identical benchmark fixture was copied. Candidate library also contains unrelated uncommitted grouped SINGLE_VALUE optimization, which is unused by JSON aggregation plans.
This is planner admission using unchanged native JSON array update and checkpoint operations, already covered by string_group_aggregates Criterion. No new native kernel is introduced.
These bounded per-key arrays do not establish behavior or performance for arbitrarily large arrays; separately paired stock controls quantify drift between JVMs.

Two additional complete-job controls load the frozen prior native library with candidate planner/classes, proving that JSON ordering admission accelerates through unchanged pre-existing native operations and does not depend on the unshipped SINGLE_VALUE work. All twenty additional warmup/measured jobs are retained.
reproduction: SF_BENCHMARK=true JAVA_HOME=<JDK17> mvn -pl streamfusion-runtime surefire:test -Pbench -Dsf.testForks=1 -Dtest=StringAggregateBenchmark -Dstringagg.function=JSON_ARRAYAGG -Dstringagg.width=16 -Dstringagg.warmup=2 -Dstringagg.runs=3 -Dsf.extraJvmArgs=-Xmx2g -Dstringagg.value=<string|bigint> -Dstringagg.order=<ASC|DESC> -Dstringagg.updating=<false|true> -Dstringagg.rows=<rows> -Dstringagg.keys=<keys> (add -Dstringagg.expectNative=false on frozen prior revision)
